C0.quote: We formalize a voting model for plurality elections
C0.note: Strategic voting model with iterative best responses under plurality.

C1.quote: we prove formally the model converges with asymptotically large electorates
C1.note: Main results: convergence/equilibrium proofs (EQ), simulations on synthetic data (SI), derivation of efficient pivotal probability calculations (AL).

C2.1.value: electoral choice / vote (candidate voted for); votes
C2.1.quote: the electoral choice of elector i in iteration δ is defined as

C2.2.note: Plurality vote for a single candidate (or abstention); not a ranking or approval set.

C2.3.quote: vector ui holds normalized cardinal utilities that i would accrue

C2.4.quote: best response may differ from their sincere preference
C2.4.note: Utilities u^i and electoral choice π^i are separate objects, and strategic vote may differ from sincere preference.

C3.1.quote: autonomous agents simultaneously maximize the utility they expect from candidates
C3.1.note: All analyses model strategic expected-utility maximizing voters (sincere voting arises only as special cases).

C4.1.note: Input is a vote for a candidate, not RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR; utilities are cardinal primitives.

C5.1.note: Evaluation is by convergence and Duvergerian equilibria, not welfare/efficiency/distortion. Expected reward is the agents' own objective, not an evaluation of rules.

VOT.quote_behav: autonomous agents simultaneously maximize the utility they expect from candidates
VOT.quote_info: They know only of candidates’ latest vote shares
VOT.note: Agents know latest vote shares only, not others' preferences or choices.

C8.1.quote: ICV agents require low information and are boundedly rational
C8.1.note: Iterative simultaneous expected-utility best responses converging to pure Nash equilibrium; bounded rationality stated.

C8.2.quote: it converges to a Pure Nash Equilibrium (PNE) as electorates become large
